text: I see you have a painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg. To better understand the cause, have you recently had any insect bites, cuts, or scratches in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes, this lesion raises concern for a specific infection. Have you noticed any fever, chills, or if the redness is spreading rapidly beyond the bite site? Also, does the area feel warm to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a painful, necrotic ulcer with purplish borders following an ant bite, combined with your history of diabetes and Crohn's, is highly concerning for ecthyma gangrenosum. I need to see the lesion to assess the extent of the necrosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Right leg lesion photograph. REQUEST TEST: Blood culture and Complete Blood Count (CBC).
